summary: This excerpt from Kate Douglas Wiggin's novel (Book 11, part 76) covers several episodes in Rebecca's life. The Simpson family moves back to their hometown, and a pulpit chair, lamps and a stove go missing from the church along the way, with a lamp later traded for an old bicycle. Rebecca grows rapidly that year, forcing Miss Jane to keep lengthening her clothes until they are passed on to Jenny. Rebecca then returns to Sunnybrook Farm for a fortnight after the death of baby Mira, and finds the household sad and changed, with Hannah seeming older than aunt Jane.
one_line: Rebecca's family and village life in Book 11: the Simpsons' move, Rebecca's sudden growth, and a sorrowful visit home after baby Mira's death.
key_facts: Mr. Simpson came home in time to move his wife and children back to the town that had given them birth.
A pulpit chair, several kerosene lamps, and a small stove disappeared from the church during the Simpsons' move.
The church lamp that went missing was obtained by an ambitious young minister in exchange for an old bicycle, with no money changing hands.
Mr. Simpson rode away on the bicycle and was not seen or heard of again for many a long day.
Rebecca grew rapidly during the year, so that Miss Jane spent months lengthening skirts, sleeves, and waists.
Rebecca's dresses were sent to Sunnybrook Farm to be made over for Jenny once letting down and piecing down reached their limit.
Mira, the baby of the Randall family, died and was buried under a willow tree at Sunnybrook Farm.
Rebecca went home for a fortnight's visit after Mira's death.
Mira had been Rebecca's special charge since her birth.
The narrator observes that it is sometimes the mystery of death that brings one to a consciousness of the still greater mystery of life.
Rebecca's homecoming was sorrowful due to Mira's death, John's absence, her mother's sadness, the isolation of the little house, and its pinching economies.
John had been Rebecca's special comrade.
Hannah seemed to have grown into a woman during Rebecca's absence.
In certain ways Hannah now appeared older, soberer, and more settled than aunt Jane.
